launch_summary.summary: The entire $10,000 budget goes to a single publisher, Hearthstone Goods, where new-home and gifting kitchen buyers are furnishing the same rooms premium linen bedding belongs in; every other reviewed publisher was either a direct competitor (Northbed) or had no link to a $280 purchase moment. There is no test budget, so nothing new is being learned about placements this flight — only which of the three running ads works. Three ads run: The Gifter, The Wellness Optimizer and The Sustainability Buyer.
uncertainties: The $280 first order value is assumed, and the $84.00 target cost per new customer is built directly on it.
Ads for The Affluent Classic and The Gen Z Aesthete won't run because no placement's shoppers fit them, so two of the five angles go untested.
The plan assumes one-time purchases and a 30% allowable share of first order value; real margin and repeat purchase behavior would change the target.
questions: What is the actual average first order value for a linen sheet set?
Do customers come back for more bedding over time, or is this genuinely a one-time purchase?
What is your gross margin, so the cost per new customer can be set on real economics?
